transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah (Redwood); Marco Diaz, Sana Patel, Jared Liu (AtlasRetail)

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call and then we'll jump into the cache numbers, priya you on?
[00:08] Priya Shah: yep here, hi all.
[00:10] Marco Diaz: Marco here.
[00:12] Sana Patel: Sana here.
[00:13] Jared Liu: Jared here.
[00:15] Alex Kim: cool, so agenda — quick recap of last week's changes, current hit rates, prompt reuse plan, and then we have a follow-up on the dedicated cluster benchmark.

[00:30] Priya Shah: ok quick recap: last week we updated the prefix canonicalization rule to normalize whitespace and strip session ids, and we bumped the KV cache TTL from 10 minutes to 30 minutes in staging. We instrumented hit-rate tags so we can see both prefix and kv hits separately.
[01:02] Marco Diaz: yeah we saw an immediate uptick but not as much as we'd hoped. our dashboard shows prefix hit 32% and KV hit 6%, so combined around 38% overall. numbers are noisy depending on time of day.
[01:25] Alex Kim: thanks marco. to clarify when you say KV hit 6%, is that for cache keys that include the full prompt+context or the small shards?
[01:35] Marco Diaz: it's the full KV keys — so the de-duped prompt keys after canonicalization. the prefix hit is matching earlier parts of the prompt that are reused.

[01:50] Priya Shah: ok that matches what we instrumented. prefix hit is doing heavy lifting, KV hit low suggests prompt bodies vary more. one hypothesis is that product descriptions have dynamic tokens — prices, dates — which reduces exact key matches.
[02:12] Sana Patel: yep price tokens and user ids are a big source of variance. we thought canonicalizing would catch some but it's not comprehensive.

[02:30] Alex Kim: right — so a couple levers: stronger canonicalization (e.g., mask numbers/dates), increase TTL which helps if requests repeat across minutes, and consider approximate caching by hashing only the first N tokens or using a semantic fingerprint to group similar prompts. each has tradeoffs.
[02:55] Jared Liu: curious about approximate caching — is that something Redwood supports rn? like fuzzy match for KV?
[03:05] Priya Shah: we have a couple options — a simple approach is prefix-only keys (first 50-80 tokens), that helps if the tail is where the variance is. a more advanced path is semantic clustering — embeddings-based grouping — but that requires extra compute and changes to cache lookup.
[03:30] Marco Diaz: embeddings cluster sounds cool but might be overkill for this pilot. what about lowering granularity, like canonicalize numeric tokens to <NUM> and dates to <DATE>?
[03:43] Priya Shah: that's low-hanging fruit and we recommended that. Marco, from your team, can you produce a list of tokenization rules for the top templates?
[03:51] Marco Diaz: yes we'll do the top 200 templates.

[04:00] Alex Kim: another question on memory: TTL increase will raise memory pressure on the Redis/KV layer — Sana any thoughts on staging memory after we bump to 1 hour?
[04:12] Sana Patel: we tested 30 minutes and saw ~12% memory increase, roughly linear. If we go to 1 hour we should expect ~25% more. we need to ensure eviction policies are ok; also check dedicated node sizing.

[04:35] Priya Shah: also consider partial eviction by prefix popularity — keep top-K prefixes pinned. we can provide suggestions based on access logs.
[04:46] Marco Diaz: what's the bootstrap plan? we had a cold-start problem early in the day.
[04:52] Priya Shah: cache warming — we can prepopulate from recent production logs or run a synthetic fanout to warm top prefixes before peak traffic. Redwood can run a one-off warm job.

[05:10] Alex Kim: ok let's review the benchmark results you sent, Priya — the 12-hour run on hosted showed combined hit up to 42% at off-peak, but during peak dropped to 30%. any notes?
[05:25] Priya Shah: yes that was on hosted with our standard kernel. variability seems tied to session-affiliated calls and campaign spikes (promo content). When we isolate promo traffic, hit rates are lower because messages include unique codes.
[05:40] Marco Diaz: so for promos we might want to bypass cache or use shorter TTL. That would avoid stale hits or incorrect reuse.

[05:55] Jared Liu: question about correctness — if we do approximate caching or prefix-only keys, do we risk returning wrong completions? how do we guarantee correctness?
[06:05] Priya Shah: good point. approximate strategies are heuristic — we recommend conservative TTLs and validation in the app layer. for prefix-only we only reuse earlier KV outputs if the model response is not critical or we use a quick post-filter. And we suggest toggling on a canary route to monitor quality impact.

[06:30] Alex Kim: quality monitoring — we have Redwood Optimize eval hooks. we can tie regression alerts to a prompt set. Marco, do you have an eval set to run against?
[06:40] Marco Diaz: yes we have 250 canonical prompts we consider critical. we'll share them.

[06:46] Priya Shah: great. Next, dedicated cluster benchmark — we recommended moving the 24h run to a dedicated pool with the optimized kernels because batching and KV sharding behave slightly differently. The dedicated run last week showed 8-12% better throughput and similar hit rates.
[07:06] Sana Patel: did memory behavior change on dedicated?
[07:09] Priya Shah: slightly better cache locality; we saw fewer evictions because shards are local to GPU memory in that setup. but configuration needs validation.

[07:25] Alex Kim: ok so concrete plan: Priya will run a 24h dedicated benchmark with TTL at 30 and 60 minutes and report TTL vs mem vs hit curve. Marco will canonicalize prompts. Alex will share dashboard and changes. Sana will validate memory. Jared will keep product aligned.

[07:50] Marco Diaz: small question: how do you measure prefix vs KV hits in the logs? I'm seeing overlapping labels.
[07:57] Priya Shah: we tag at lookup time — prefix_hit means the prefix matcher returned an early token-level match and we streamed from cache; kv_hit means the full KV key returned a cached completion. there can be overlap in that a prefix hit may still lead to a KV lookup; we count both separately which can look additive.
[08:20] Marco Diaz: ok that explains it, perhaps we need a combined unique-hit metric.

[08:30] Alex Kim: also discussed prompt reuse strategy — beyond canonicalization: 1) canonical templates for user-facing messages, 2) server-side token masking, 3) use of shorter fixed prompts where possible, 4) implement a light-weight hashing scheme of first 64 tokens. Which of these are feasible?
[08:50] Marco Diaz: we can do 1 and 2 quickly; hashing first 64 tokens maybe fine but we need to validate collisions.

[09:00] Priya Shah: we'll provide a small validation harness to check collision rate for hashed prefix keys on your corpus.

[09:10] Jared Liu: any security considerations? we need to ensure no PII falls into shared cache keys.
[09:18] Alex Kim: yes we recommend stripping PII at canonicalization time and using customer-scoped caches (we're using VPC-isolated KV for AtlasRetail). keys are never shared across customers.

[09:30] Sana Patel: also need to confirm KMS usage for any persisted cache snapshots — internal compliance will want to see encryption at rest for Redis/AOF backups.
[09:40] Priya Shah: confirmed — Redwood Private/Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS and we record audit logs. I'll attach the security brief.

[09:55] Alex Kim: ok last bit — rollout and monitoring. We'll canary approximate caching on 5% traffic first, tie regression alerts to the 250 eval prompts, and have a quick rollback plan. Sound good?
[10:05] Marco Diaz: yes.
[10:07] Jared Liu: yes.

[10:10] Alex Kim: great. recap of next steps and owners — I'll send notes and timeline. anything else?
[10:16] Marco Diaz: one ask — can Redwood share a short doc on prefix hashing tradeoffs?
[10:20] Priya Shah: yes we'll send a 1-pager.
[10:23] Alex Kim: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the benchmark results and the canonicalization mapping.
[10:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcript is auto-generated; occasional words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" or "k v cache"), punctuation is rough. Links referenced in call: caching dashboard - https://redwood.internal/dashboard/atlas/caching (private), security brief link: (shared via email).
